function: Excluded (above_phy): DRL (PPO) decides network slicing, slice and user computing and bandwidth shares, and UAV trajectory for task offloading in UAV-enabled MEC (pp. 2, 7).
notes: Checks 1-3 pass: a research article with a learned method (two-timescale PPO) and quantitative results (Fig. 5, Fig. 7). Exclusion is above_phy: the learned actions are the slice-level shares of computing and bandwidth, the user-level shares of computing and bandwidth, and the UAV trajectory (p. 7, Eqs. 14-15); the reward is the negative of a cost made of resource consumption, slice reconfiguration, task failure and UAV energy (pp. 6-7); the conclusion says 'we focus on the dynamic heterogeneous computing task offloading problem for UAV-enabled edge computing based on network slicing techniques' (p. 13). No transmit power, beam or modulation is learned: the terminal power in Eq. (3) (p. 5) is not an action, and Table I (p. 11) lists RL hyperparameters, antenna gains, a path loss index and the wavelength only. Doubt for the reviewer: in aerial links, learned resource allocation counts as physical layer (step 1, code 4); if the learned bandwidth shares (alpha_B, beta_B, p. 7) are read as such, the work passes this check and would fall in area 6, where single-antenna links are admitted.
